    People also ask
    Is Vanderbilt an Ivy League school?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    No,
    Vanderbilt University is not an Ivy League school. The Ivy League consists of eight specific Northeastern private institutions (Brown, Columbia, Cornell, Dartmouth, Harvard, Penn, Princeton, and Yale). However, Vanderbilt is considered a "New Ivy" or "Hidden Ivy" due to its comparable academic, prestige, and selective admission standards, featuring acceptance rates under 6%. 
    Key Details About Vanderbilt's Standing: 
    • Not an Ivy: Vanderbilt was founded in 1872 in the South and is not part of the historic athletic conference that defines the Ivy League.
    • "New Ivy" Designation: Forbes and other educational experts have listed Vanderbilt among the "New Ivies"—elite universities with academic rigor and selectivity similar to traditional Ivies.
    • Selective Admissions:
      With a 5.8% acceptance rate for the Class of 2028, it is as selective as many Ivy League schools, notes this Instagram post.
    • Prestige: It is often considered a "Southern Ivy" or "Ivy Plus" university, as discussed on this Facebook page , offering top-tier research, faculty, and career outcomes, notes this Quora post.
